lede: Barry Martin's Hopalong strange attractor, rendered live on the Super Nintendo and flown around with the joypad — written in C and compiled to a real .sfc ROM with the llvm-mos-based 65816 toolchain. The attractor accumulates into a hit-count grid in WRAM and shows through Mode 7, with the parameter panel spliced in by an HDMA mode-switch.

The three attractors

Cycle them with X (next) / A (previous) — each is a distinct bounded Hopalong shape; switching re-blooms the cloud (~10 s).

Tips

  • The bloom is the point. After boot or an attractor switch the cloud fills in over ~10 s; once it's in, the motion is the palette shimmer.
  • Zoom pivots on the attractor (Q/W), so it stays put as you zoom; the D-pad slides it around and Enter snaps back.
  • Colour modes (Shift) rotate where the hue wheel starts — the shape is unchanged.

Built in C with an LLVM/65816 SNES toolchain, verified pixel-for-pixel against two emulators. The player above is that exact cycle-accurate core — hit Verify fidelity to reproduce the build gate's WRAM assert (grid hash 0x9047) live in this tab.
